questions.stem: What is the independent variable in this core practical?

options.text: the frequency of the tuning fork chosen
options.explanation: Different tuning forks supply the input frequencies.

options.text: the loudness of the hum test
options.explanation: The hum only checks the microphone works.

options.text: the number of divisions on the screen
options.explanation: That is part of the reading, not the input.

options.text: the time period of the wave
options.explanation: Time period is the dependent variable being measured.

questions.stem: Why is the time base adjusted before striking the fork?

options.text: to make the trace taller
options.explanation: The vertical gain changes height, not the time base.

options.text: so that multiple complete waves fit on the screen
options.explanation: The method requires several full cycles to be visible before measuring.

options.text: to silence background noise
options.explanation: The time base does not filter sound.

options.text: to change the fork’s frequency
options.explanation: The fork’s frequency is fixed by its construction.

questions.stem: How is the time period read from the frozen trace?

options.text: measure the height of the tallest peak
options.explanation: Height gives amplitude, not period.

options.text: read the frequency directly off the screen
options.explanation: The screen shows the waveform; the frequency is calculated.

options.text: count the divisions spanned by one complete wave cycle
options.explanation: One full cycle across the divisions, converted by the time base, is the period.

options.text: count the divisions spanned by all visible waves
options.explanation: All visible waves span several periods, not one.

questions.stem: A time base is set in ms per centimetre. A wave spans 4 cm for one cycle with a time base of 1 ms/cm. What is the frequency?

options.explanation: This treats 4 ms as if it were already inverted in kHz.
This slips a factor of a thousand on the unit conversion.

options.text: 4 Hz
options.explanation: 4 ms is the period; inverting gives the frequency, not this value.

options.text: 250 Hz

questions.stem: Why is the microphone tested by humming before the forks are used?

options.text: to check the microphone displays a signal
options.explanation: The hum confirms the microphone and scope chain works before measurements start.

options.text: to set the fork frequency
options.explanation: Humming does not tune anything.

options.text: to clean the microphone
options.explanation: Cleaning is unrelated to the hum test.

options.text: to warm up the oscilloscope screen
options.explanation: Screens do not need humming.

questions.stem: State the dependent variable of this experiment.
questions.modelAnswer: The dependent variable is the time period of the displayed wave.

questions.stem: State the equation used to convert the measured time period into frequency.
questions.modelAnswer: Frequency = 1 divided by time period, f = 1/T.

questions.stem: Explain why several complete waves should be visible on the screen before a reading is taken.
questions.modelAnswer: With several complete cycles on screen the one chosen for measurement can be a clean, representative cycle, the scale can be checked for consistency across cycles, and a single clipped or distorted cycle cannot masquerade as a full period.

questions.stem: A fork’s trace spans 3 divisions for one cycle at a time base of 2 ms per division. Calculate the frequency of the fork.
